info.title: TelltaleDNS API
info.description: Read and control a TelltaleDNS resolver. JSON is camelCase; field names carry units (`totalMs`, `ttlSeconds`). Errors are RFC 9457 problem+json with a stable `code` and a `hint`. Time parameters take RFC 3339 or a relative offset (`-24h`). Collections page with `cursor`/`limit`. Analytics calls take `scope` (`cluster` or `node:local`; both mean this node until clustering is available).

get.description:
The alerts firing at this moment and the last delivery to each destination (with its
error, if it failed). Rules are checked on the cluster's primary; on another node
`evaluating` is false. The destinations and rules themselves are configuration:
`GET /api/v1/config/entries?kind=alert_destination` and `kind=alert_rule`.

put.summary: Add or change an alert destination (OBS-010, T9.6).
put.description:
The body has the same fields as `[[alerts.destination]]` (the name comes from the path):
`{"type": "ntfy", "url": "https://ntfy.sh/my-topic"}`, or for email
`{"type": "email", "url": "smtp://smtp.gmail.com:587", "from": "me@gmail.com", "to":
["me@gmail.com"], "username": "me@gmail.com", "password_file": "/run/secrets/smtp"}`.
Secrets stay in files on the node (`token_file`, `password_file`): only the path is sent.
A destination the config files define is overridden until this one is deleted.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

200.description: Applied (or, with dryRun, what would change).

412.description: The configuration changed since the If-Match version: re-read it and retry.

422.description: A field is wrong, or the configuration wouldn't be valid: problem+json says which.

delete.description: Rules that still send to it make the configuration invalid (422 says which).

post.summary: Send a test alert to one destination (OBS-010, T9.6).
post.description:
Sends a message marked as a test, from this node, and answers with what happened: `ok`, or
the destination's error (a wrong password, an unreachable server). Nothing is stored, but
the test is audited. Needs the operator role.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The destination.

`upstream_down`, `node_down`, `list_failing`, `anomaly`, `servfail_rate`,
`update_available`, `sync_lag`, `new_device`, `disk_full`, `plan_pending`.

get.summary: Device anomalies: rate spikes, heavy volume to one domain, drift, beaconing (OBS-013).
get.description:
Each finding compares a device with its own learned baseline (after a learning period,
7 days by default) and carries the evidence: observed value, usual value ± spread, the
threshold, and the window. Findings are alert-only; TelltaleDNS never blocks on them.
Newest first. In a cluster every node's findings are included (each node learns from the
queries it answers), with `nodes` saying which found each. Each has a stable `id` for
acknowledging it (OBS-014); `acknowledged` says who did and when, and `acknowledged=false`
returns only the ones nobody has.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only findings whose window started after this (RFC 3339 or relative, default `-7d`).

parameters.name: acknowledged
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-014 — `false`: only findings nobody acknowledged; `true`: only acknowledged
ones. Default: both.

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says which parameter and how to fix it.

post.description:
Marks findings as seen, by their `id` from `GET /analytics/anomalies`: the sidebar badge and
`acknowledged=false` stop counting them, and each shows who acknowledged it and when. In a
cluster the primary records it (any node forwards) and every node shows it within seconds,
including nodes that were down, when they reconnect. Acknowledging changes no configuration,
so it works in a GitOps-managed cluster too. Findings keep being reported as before.
Needs the operator role (agents: the `ops:anomalies` scope); audit-logged as `anomaly.ack`.

400.description: No IDs, too many, a malformed one, or a long note.

503.description: A replica that can't reach the primary.

post.summary: Take back acknowledgements of device anomalies.
post.description:
The findings count in the badge again. Same rules as acknowledging; audit-logged as
`anomaly.unack`.

200.description: How many acknowledgements were taken back.

400.description: No IDs, too many, or a malformed one.

503.description: A replica that can't reach the primary.

get.summary: Domains devices contacted for the first time (OBS-009).
get.description:
Each device's first-seen registrable domains (after its first day, so the initial learning
doesn't flood the feed), with a score for how machine-generated the name looks (DGA
likelihood, 0 to 1). Newest first. A device that contacts several high-scoring new domains
in an hour also shows up in `/analytics/anomalies` as `dga`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only domains first seen after this (RFC 3339 or relative, default `-24h`).

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: Only this device (its address).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many (default 200, at most 2000).

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says which parameter and how to fix it.

get.description:
Blocked names that look like they shouldn't be, best first (at most `limit`, default 50):
`allowedAfterBlock` counts devices that got the name answered normally within 10 minutes of
a block (someone paused blocking or allowed it: the strongest sign), `retryBursts` the times
a device asked for it 10 or more times within a minute while blocked (apps that break retry;
ad libraries do too, so weigh it lower). With the lists that blocked it. Since start; every
node's, merged by name. Names follow the query-log privacy level.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many (1–500, default 50).

get.summary: What the shadow lists would have blocked.
get.description:
A list with `mode = "shadow"` is compiled and checked but never blocks. For each query
answered normally, the telemetry thread checks it against the device's group's shadow lists
too; this is what they would have blocked since start: queries, devices, the names most
often, the last one. Every list in shadow mode is listed (with zero until it would block
something). Use it to judge a new list before turning it on. In a cluster, every node's
counts add up. Names follow the query-log privacy level.

200.description: One entry per list in shadow mode.

get.summary: Upstream answer quality and second opinions.
get.description:
Per node, per upstream since start: the DNSSEC verdicts on its answers (when validating),
the Extended DNS Error codes it returned (EDE 15 Blocked, 16 Censored, 17 Filtered mean the
upstream filters), and, when `[upstream_check] sample_every` is set, how sampled answers
compared with a second upstream's: `same`, `differentAddresses` (CDNs and geo-DNS answer per
resolver, usually harmless), `differentRcode`, `filtered` (one side had addresses, the other
none or only 0.0.0.0/loopback), or `unanswered`. `recent` lists the latest disagreements with
both answers. Names follow the query-log privacy level.

get.summary: Analytics over the query log in one query (`vqlog`, AGT-012).
get.description:
A small pipe language: `from -24h | where status = blocked and group = kids | top 10 name`,
`from -7d | where client = 192.168.1.20 | bucket 1h | stats count, p95(latency)`,
`where name under roku.com | by client | stats count, distinct(name)`. Stages: `from TIME
[to TIME]`, `where FIELD OP VALUE [and …]` (fields name, client, group, status, qtype,
rcode, upstream, proto, latency, `upstream_latency`; ops =, !=, in (…), not in (…), and for
names ~ glob, has, under; for latencies >, >=, <, <= in ms), `bucket 5m|1h|1d`, `by KEY,
…` (name, domain, client, group, status, qtype, rcode, upstream, proto), `stats count,
distinct(KEY), avg|min|max|p50|p90|p95|p99(latency|upstream_latency|answers|bytes)`, `top N
KEY`, `sort COLUMN [asc|desc]`, `limit N` (≤ 200). The answer is a table, the query as
understood, and its cost; `dryRun=true` only estimates. Never SQL; read-only. A query that
would read more than 100 million logged queries is refused with a 400 (narrow the time or
filter).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The query, for example `from -24h | where status = blocked | top 10 name`.
parameters.example: from -24h | where status = blocked | top 10 name

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Only parse and estimate the cost; don't scan.

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says what's wrong in the query and how to fix it.

get.description:
Every change to users, passwords, two-factor sign-in, and API tokens, sign-ins and
lockouts, and configuration reloads, newest first, with who (attributed to the token and
its owner for API tokens), from where, why (`X-Telltale-Reason`), and what changed. Append-only and
hash-chained; check it with GET /audit/verify.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per page (1–500, default 100).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: From a previous page's `nextCursor`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: An action or prefix (`user.`, `token.create`).

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: Exactly this actor.

400.description: Invalid request: problem+json says which parameter and how to fix it.

403.description: Signed in, but not allowed to do this (role, token scope, or agent restriction).

get.description:
Recomputes every entry's hash and link. `ok: false` with `firstBadSeq` means the log was
edited at or before that entry outside TelltaleDNS. Compare `headHash` with a value you
saved earlier to detect removed entries at the end.

403.description: Signed in, but not allowed to do this (role, token scope, or agent restriction).

post.description:
Username and password, plus `totp` (or `recoveryCode`) when two-factor sign-in is on:
without it the answer is 401 `totp_required`. Sets an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict` session
cookie and returns the CSRF token to send as `X-CSRF-Token` on changes. Repeated failures
lock the username and the address out for a while (429). At most four password checks run
at once; beyond that the answer is 503 with Retry-After, which isn't a failed sign-in.

401.description: Not signed in, or the credentials are wrong.

429.description: Too many requests: wait for Retry-After seconds.

503.description: Busy checking other sign-ins: retry after Retry-After seconds (not counted as a failure).

post.description: Ends this session and clears the cookie. With a token or Basic, does nothing but succeed.

200.description: Signed out of an OIDC session: send the browser to `logoutUrl` to sign out at the provider too.

get.description:
The signed-in user: role (capped by a token's scope), two-factor state, unused recovery
codes, and how this request authenticated.

The provider returns here with `code` and `state`. Validates both, exchanges the code,
verifies the ID token, maps groups to a role (creating the user on first sign-in), sets
the session cookie, and redirects to the UI. Failures redirect to `/#/?loginError=...`.
Register `<public_url>/api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/callback` with the provider.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Provider ID

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The authorization code from the provider.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The value TelltaleDNS sent at the start, checked against the sign-in cookie.

parameters.name: error
parameters.description: Set instead of `code` when the user cancelled or the provider refused.

parameters.name: error_description
parameters.description: The provider's explanation of `error`.

302.description: Signed in (to the UI), or back to sign-in with `loginError`.

get.summary: Start signing in with an OIDC provider.
get.description:
Redirects the browser to the provider (Authorization Code + PKCE). The provider sends it
back to `/api/v1/auth/oidc/{id}/callback`, which signs in and returns to `returnTo`.
Browsers only: link a "Sign in with ..." button here.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Provider ID

parameters.name: returnTo
parameters.description: UI route to return to after sign-in (`/#/queries`). Default `/#/`.

503.description: Not available on this node right now.

post.description: Needs the current password. Ends every other session of this user.

401.description: Not signed in, or the credentials are wrong.

post.description:
Only while no user exists. `setupToken` is saved in `<data_dir>/setup-token` at startup
(`telltale auth setup-token` prints it; the log names the file, not the token). Signs the
new admin in (sets the session cookie).

401.description: Not signed in, or the credentials are wrong.

get.description:
Whether first-run setup is needed, and who the request is signed in as (if anyone),
with the session's CSRF token. Public; the UI calls it on load.

post.description: Needs the current password. Removes the TOTP secret and the unused recovery codes.

401.description: Not signed in, or the credentials are wrong.

post.description:
Confirms a current code from the app enrolled with POST /auth/totp/setup, turns
enforcement on, and returns ten single-use recovery codes (shown only now).

401.description: Not signed in, or the credentials are wrong.

post.description:
Returns a new TOTP secret (base32 and an `otpauth://` URL for a QR code). Nothing is
enforced until POST /auth/totp/enable confirms a code from the app.

409.description: Conflicts with the current state: problem+json says what to change.

get.summary: Download a backup of this node.
get.description:
One `.ttbk` file (ADR-063) with the configuration files, users and API tokens, devices and
names made through the API, the audit log, statistics history, and anomaly baselines.
Sign-in sessions, lists, and the cluster identity aren't included, and neither is the
query log (use `telltale backup create --include-qlog` for that). Restore it with
`telltale backup restore FILE` on the new machine.

The file holds password hashes: keep it private. Admin only; audited as `backup.create`.

200.description: The backup, as an attachment named `telltale-<node>-<time>.ttbk`.

503.description: Backups aren't available on this node.

get.summary: Whether blocking is paused, per node.
get.description:
For each node: its active pauses (everyone, or one group) and when each ends. Nothing listed
means blocking is on.

post.description:
Turns blocking off for `minutes` (1 to 1,440; agents at most 60) for everyone, or only for
`group`'s devices, then it turns back on by itself. Every node pauses, unless `node` names
one. Quick rules that block stop too; local names, forwarding, and allow rules don't change.
Needs the operator role (agents: the `ops:pause` scope); audit-logged as `blocking.pause`.

400.description: No or too many minutes, an unknown group, or an unknown node.
An unknown group or node.

get.summary: The cache's top entries and makeup, per node.
get.description:
For each node: what its cache holds by kind (answers, NXDOMAIN, no data, SERVFAIL, stale,
DNSSEC-validated), and its `limit` entries with the most hits, the largest, or the fresh
ones closest to expiring. Each node walks its cache once for this (a few milliseconds per
100,000 entries, off the query path); looking doesn't count as a hit. A node that couldn't
be asked is listed with the error.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `hits` (default), `bytes`, or `expiring` (fresh answers closest to expiring).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries per node, 1 to 200 (default 25).

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: One node only (its site, pod, or ID); absent: every node.

400.description: An unknown sort or node.

post.summary: Flush the cache: one name, a subtree, or everything.
post.description:
With `name`, removes that name's cached answers (with `subtree`, every name under it too);
without, empties the cache. By default every node in the cluster flushes; `node` limits it to
one. The next query for a flushed name is asked of the upstreams again. This doesn't clear
devices' own caches, blocked answers are never cached (unblocking needs no flush), and to
change what a name resolves to, use local names instead. Needs the operator role (or the
`ops:cache` agent scope); audit-logged as `cache.flush`.

400.description: Not a domain name, or an unknown node.

get.summary: What the cache holds for a name, on every node.
get.description:
Each cached answer for exactly `name` (every query type, and the variants for clients that
set DO or CD), with the node that holds it, its response code, answer count, whether it was
DNSSEC-validated, how long it stays fresh (negative: how long it has been stale), its age,
size, and hits. Looking doesn't count as a hit or change anything. Blocked answers are never
cached, so they don't appear.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name to look up, e.g. `www.example.com`.

200.description: The cached answers (empty when there are none).

400.description: Not a domain name.

get.description:
For each node (this one first): entries, memory, hits, misses, the hit rate, stale answers
served, prefetches, evictions, and answers that couldn't be cached. Each node has its own
cache, so a cluster shows one row per node.

post.summary: Check a draft list before saving it (API-002, T9.12).
post.description:
The body has the same fields as `PUT /api/v1/lists/{name}` (`name` optional): a `url` is
downloaded from this node (with `[filter]`'s size limit and timeout), or `rules` are taken
as they are, then parsed as the compiler would. Answers with the rules found, the lines it
couldn't use, and the time. Nothing is saved or compiled; the check is audited. `path`
lists are checked when saved. Needs the operator role (agents: `config:write:lists`).

422.description: The body isn't a list (an unknown or mistyped field), or it has no url or rules.

post.summary: Check a draft upstream before saving it (API-002, T9.12).
post.description:
The body has the same fields as `PUT /api/v1/upstreams/{name}` (`name` optional). This node
builds it and asks it for the root's NS records, as health checks do, and answers with what
happened: `ok` with the rcode, records, and time, or the error (a bad URL, a TLS name that
doesn't match, a timeout). Nothing is saved; the check is audited. Needs the operator role
(agents: `config:write:upstreams`).

422.description: The body isn't an upstream (an unknown or mistyped field).

get.summary: Configured clients (devices) and how they're recognized.
get.description:
Each device's name, the IPs, CIDRs, MACs, or client IDs that identify it, and its groups in
priority order (the first group's settings apply). Unknown devices use the `default` group.

put.summary: Create, rename, or change a device (API-010).
put.description:
Names devices across every view: the query log, live tail, charts, and history (names
are resolved when read, so earlier queries are relabelled too). To rename, send the new
`name` in the body. Devices defined in the config files are read-only here (409). Needs
the operator role (or a `write` token).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The device's current name (or the name for a new one).

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

200.description: Applied (or, with dryRun, what would change).

409.description: Defined in the config files, or an Idempotency-Key reused for another request.

412.description: If-Match: the config changed since that version.

422.description: The resulting configuration is invalid (e.g. an unknown group).

delete.summary: Delete a device named through the API.
delete.description:
Its queries, past and future, go back to showing the address, and it leaves its groups
(the `default` group applies). Devices from the config files can't be deleted here (409).
Needs the operator role (or a `write` token).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The device's name.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

404.description: No device by that name was created through the API.

412.description: The configuration changed since the If-Match version: re-read it and retry.

get.description:
Every node this node knows: role, link state and round-trip time, configuration version
and lag, and whether it's serving DNS (queries per second, SERVFAIL share, upstream p90).
Plus `checks` (each with a plain-language fix when failing) and recent `events`. On a
standalone node, `enabled` is false. Use it to answer "is the cluster healthy and serving?".

post.description:
Manual failover (ADR-051): use when the primary is gone. The node takes a new epoch,
publishes the cluster's configuration from the last version it applied, and every node
follows it. An old primary that comes back steps down, and anything it changed meanwhile
shows under `conflicts`.

Refused when:
- the current primary is up;
- the node isn't eligible or lacks the cluster key;
- without `emergency`, the cluster takes its configuration from Git and this node isn't
  managed from Git.

With `?dryRun=true`, nothing changes: the checks run and the answer is a `PromotePlan`
(the epoch, whether it would be an emergency primary, and a sentence on what would happen).

Admin only; audited as `cluster.promote`. From a signed-in session it needs `password`
(and `totp` with two-factor sign-in on); API tokens don't.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Check and report without changing anything.

200.description: Promoted; the cluster as it is now. With `dryRun=true`: a `PromotePlan` instead, and nothing changed.

400.description: A signed-in session didn't send `password`.

401.description: Not signed in, or two-factor sign-in is on and `totp` is missing (`totp_required`).

403.description: The password or code is wrong, or not an admin.

409.description: Not allowed now (the primary is up, or this node can't be primary).

429.description: Too many wrong passwords: wait for Retry-After seconds.

get.summary: The configuration's upstreams, upstream groups, lists, and groups, with their sources.
get.description:
Each definition in effect, with the same fields as in `telltale.toml`, and where it comes
from (ADR-069): `file`, `added` (made through the UI or API), `override` (replaces the
config files' entry of the same name), or `hidden` (the files' entry is left out; listed so
it can be brought back). `DELETE` on an override's or a hidden entry's path brings the
files' version back. Secrets aren't part of these sections.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: One kind only: `upstream`, `upstream_group`, `list`, or `group`.

200.description: The entries, by kind and name.

get.summary: Devices found on the network (API-010; T8.2, T8.3).
get.description:
The DHCP clients of the routers TelltaleDNS reads (`[[router]]`: UniFi, OPNsense), then the
names devices announce over mDNS (`[clients] mdns`), each with the name the device has in
TelltaleDNS. TelltaleDNS doesn't run a DHCP server itself (ADR-091); the path keeps its name
because these are the router's DHCP leases.

put.summary: Keep names and devices out of the query log and analytics (OBS-022).
put.description:
The body has the same fields as `[exclusions]` in `telltale.toml`: `enabled` (turn them on or
off without losing the lists), `names` (each with its subdomains, e.g.
`connectivitycheck.gstatic.com`), and `clients` (addresses or networks). Their queries are
still answered and still counted in `/metrics`, but left out of the query log, the live view,
the dashboard and top lists, anomalies, and every export. It replaces the whole section until
it's deleted again; it applies to every node of a cluster from the next query on.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: Validate and report the change without applying it.

parameters.name: simulate
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — with `dryRun=true`: replay the query log over this window (`24h`,
`7d`; at most 7 days; `true` for `[simulate] default_window`) and report what the
change would have done to those queries (`simulation`). `auto`: only when
`[simulate] plans_by_default` is on.

parameters.name: simulateUntil
parameters.description:
REQ: OBS-024 — where the simulated window ends: RFC 3339 or relative (`-24h`).
Default now.

`[node] maintenance_default_secs`, 3,600) the node answers `/readyz` with 503 so load
balancers and Kubernetes stop sending it new queries, while every DNS listener keeps
answering whatever still arrives. Its alerts and health conditions are left out, and it
doesn't stand in elections, until the window ends (by itself, or with DELETE). The window
survives a restart. Starting again replaces the window. `id` is `local` (the node answering)
or a cluster node's ID, site, or pod name: the request goes to that node over the cluster
channel. On the primary under automatic failover, `handover` (default true) hands the primary
role to another eligible node first (configuration changes pause for about 30 s); otherwise
the primary keeps the role and the answer's `note` says to promote another node first. It
changes no configuration, so a GitOps-managed cluster takes it too. Needs the operator role
(agents: the `ops:maintenance` scope); audit-logged as `node.maintenance.start`.

oidcProvider.description: The sign-in provider for users created by OIDC sign-in (they have no password here).

totp.description: 6-digit code from the authenticator app, when TOTP is on.

csrfToken.description: Send as `X-CSRF-Token` on every change made with this session.

logoutUrl.description: Send the browser here to also sign out at the provider.

forSecs.description:
How long, in seconds: 60 to 86,400 (agents at most 7,200). Default: the node's
`[node] maintenance_default_secs` (3,600).

handover.description:
For the primary under automatic failover: hand the primary role to another eligible
node first (about 30 s without configuration changes). Default true; ignored on other
nodes.

reason.description:
Why, in a few words (1 to 200 characters, one line). Shown on the Cluster page, in the
health panel, and in the audit log.

MaintenanceResult.description: A node's maintenance after a start or end.

handover.description:
Starting on the primary: `started` (another node is being elected; the old primary
follows), `unavailable` (manual failover, or no other eligible node reachable: it stays
the primary), or `declined` (`handover: false`). `not_needed` on other nodes.

node.description: The node (its pod, site, or ID).

note.description: What to know, in one sentence (e.g. promote another node first).

oneOf.description: The window, while active.

MaskedClients.description: Evidence that client IPs appear masked.

sharePercent.description: Share of the window's queries sent by `sources`, in percent (> 90).

sources.description: The infrastructure addresses that sent them, heaviest first (at most 3).

recoveryCodesLeft.description: Unused recovery codes (when TOTP is on).

role.description: Effective role (a token's scope caps its owner's role).

NewDomain.description: A registrable domain a device contacted for the first time (REQ: OBS-009).

dgaScore.description: How machine-generated its name looks, 0 to 1 (0.6 and up is suspicious; `06` §7).

token.description: The token, shown only now: send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

NodeMaintenance.description:
REQ: OPS-010 (ADR-118) — a node's maintenance window: it reports not ready (balancers stop
sending it new queries), keeps answering, and is left out of alerts, the health level, and
elections until `until`.

by.description: Who started it: a user, `<user> via <site>` from another node, or an agent.

node.description: The node (its pod, site, or ID), in lists.

OverblockSuspect.description:
REQ: OBS-018 (ADR-109) — a blocked name that looks like it shouldn't be: devices kept
retrying it, or it was answered normally soon after being blocked (someone paused
blocking or allowed it).

allowedAfterBlock.description:
Times a device got it answered normally within 10 minutes of a block (a pause, a
quick allow, or an allowlist entry: someone wanted it).

devices.description: Devices involved (none counted at privacy level 2 and above).

name.description: Hashed at privacy level 1 and above.

retryBursts.description:
Times a device asked for it 10 or more times within a minute while it was blocked
(apps that break retry; ad libraries do too).

configVersion.description: The configuration version the plan was made against.

method.description: The REST write it replays: `PUT` or `DELETE`.

preview.description: The dry run's answer: before, after, impact, and warnings.

reason.description: Why the agent wants it (goes into the audit log).

result.description: The write's answer once applied (or why it failed).

state.description:
`pending` (waits for an operator), `ready`, `approved`, `rejected`, `applying`,
`applied`, `stale` (the configuration changed), `failed`, `discarded`, or `expired`.

summary.description: What it does, in one sentence.

tool.description: The MCP tool that made it, e.g. `plan_block_domain`.

ProbeResult.description:
REQ: OBS-020 (ADR-107) — one synthetic probe: a DNS listener asked through its own
protocol, or an extra target, from one node, and the listener's certificate.

certError.description: Why the certificate couldn't be read.

certExpiresUnixSeconds.description: A TLS listener's certificate: when it expires and the days left (negative: expired).

consecutiveFailures.description: Probes failed in a row (2 or more degrade the health level).

lastOkUnixSeconds.description: When it last answered, and when it was last asked (Unix seconds).

listener.description: One of this node's listeners (else an extra `[probe] targets` entry).

node.description: The node that probed (cluster nodes only).

ok.description: The last probe got a well-formed answer (any response code).

skipped.description: Not probed, and why (a listener that requires the PROXY protocol header).

detail.description: What went wrong in this request.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

example.detail: `from`: `yesterday`: expected RFC 3339 time (2026-10-03T12:00:00Z) or a relative offset (-24h)
example.hint: Use a relative offset such as -24h, or RFC 3339 such as 2026-10-03T00:00:00Z.
example.title: Invalid parameter

PromotePlan.description: What promoting this node would do (`POST /cluster/promote?dryRun=true`, AGT-002).

emergency.description: It would coordinate without publishing new configuration (ADR-048).

epoch.description: The epoch this node would take.

impact.description: What would happen, in one sentence.

emergency.description:
Promote even though this node can't publish configuration under the cluster's
authority (configuration from Git, and no Git-managed node reachable): it coordinates the
cluster and keeps the last version, and publishes nothing new (ADR-048).

password.description:
From a signed-in session: your password, to confirm (`spec/12` §5). Not needed with
an API token or for `dryRun`.

totp.description: From a signed-in session with two-factor sign-in on: the current code.

QueryPage.description: A page of query-log rows, newest first.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read (CLU-002: partial results, never a hang).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get older rows; absent when there are none.

scanned.description: How much of the log this page looked at.

clientName.description: The configured device name, when known.

list.description: The list whose rule blocked or allowed the query.

node.description: The node that answered it (federated reads: its site).

rcode.description: Response code, or null when nothing was sent.

RecordInput.description: One record of a local name.

value.description:
An address for A/AAAA, a name for CNAME/PTR, text for TXT, `"10 mail.home.arpa"` for MX,
`"0 5 5060 pbx.home.arpa"` for SRV.

answer.description: An address, or a name (answered as a CNAME).

RuleInfo.description: A quick rule (files and API), with how long it has left.

expiresInSeconds.description: Seconds until it expires (0 once it has).

RuleInput.description:
REQ: FLT-005 (T6.12, ADR-067) — a quick rule to create or replace
(`PUT /api/v1/rules/{id}`).

devices.description: Device names, IPs, or CIDRs it applies to.

domain.description: The domain; its subdomains are included.

expires.description: When it stops applying (RFC 3339). Use this or `forMinutes`; neither means never.

forMinutes.description: Stop applying this many minutes from now.

groups.description: Groups it applies to. With neither devices nor groups: everyone.

note.description: Why it exists, shown with every decision it makes.

Scope.description: An API token's scope; a token never exceeds its owner's role.

domains.description: The domains it blocks (with everything under them).

ShadowListStats.description:
REQ: OBS-018 (ADR-109) — what a `shadow` list would have blocked (it never does), since
the node started (every node's, merged, in a cluster).

devices.description: Devices those queries came from (each node counts its own; capped at 4,096 per node).

hits.description: Queries it would have blocked (answered normally instead).

nodes.description: The nodes that counted (cluster nodes only).

since.description: When counting started (RFC 3339): the earliest node's start, in a cluster.

topNames.description: The names it would have blocked most (hashed at privacy level 1 and above).

config.description:
The candidate shared configuration, as JSON: the shape a Git commit's shared TOML
becomes (node-local sections are ignored; this node's own apply).

until.description: The end of the window (RFC 3339 or relative, e.g. `-1h`); default now.

window.description: How far back: `30m`, `24h`, `7d` (at most 7 days). Default `[simulate] default_window`.

SimulatedClass.description:
One kind of difference: how many queries, from how many devices, and the names most
affected (at most 20, most first).

list.description:
What decided: the list (or quick rule, schedule) that blocks or had blocked it, the
route change, or the new answer.

Simulation.description:
REQ: OBS-024 (T13.1, ADR-115) — what a configuration change would have done to the queries
already in the query log: each logged query decided again under the current configuration
and under the candidate, and the differences counted. Decisions only: nothing is asked of
upstreams, and caching, DNSSEC, rate limits, pauses, and CNAME-target blocks aren't replayed.
About the past: names nobody asked in the window count for nothing.

applicable.description:
False for a change that can't affect a decision (alerts, users, exclusions): nothing
was read.

available.description:
False when it couldn't run (`reason` says why: `disabled`, `privacy_level`,
`no_query_log`, `busy`, ...).

byDevice.description: The devices most affected, most first (at most 50).

changedAnswer.description:
Answered differently without a block: a local record, a rewrite, no IPv6 addresses, a
special answer (`list` describes the new answer).

changedRoute.description: Forwarded to another upstream group (`list` says from where to where).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes whose queries aren't included (they didn't answer).

newlyAllowed.description: Blocked now, allowed under the change (`list` names the list that had blocked it).

newlyBlocked.description: Allowed now, blocked under the change.

partial.description: Stopped early (`[simulate] max_rows` or `max_secs`): the counts cover the newest `rows`.

rows.description: Logged queries read (on every node that answered).

undetermined.description:
At privacy level 1 (names hashed), queries of devices whose group changes to one with
different settings: they can't be decided again without the names.

SloBurn.description:
REQ: OBS-016 — the error budget's burn rate over one window: the bad share divided by the
share the target allows (1 spends exactly the budget over the objective's window).

rate.description: None when there were no answers (or no hourly data for `3d`).

total.description: Answers in the window, and bad ones.

SloObjective.description:
REQ: OBS-016 — one objective: `availability` (answers that aren't SERVFAIL) or `latency`
(answers within `latencyMs`). Dropped queries got no answer and count for neither.

alert.description:
`fast` (14.4× over 1h and 5m), `slow` (6× over 6h and 30m), or `ticket` (1× over 3d
and 6h); none when the budget lasts. `fast` and `slow` degrade the health level and
fire `slo_burn` alerts.

budgetRemainingPercent.description: The window's error budget left, in percent: 100 untouched, 0 spent, below 0 overspent.

good.description: Good and all answers over the window.

goodMeans.description: What counts as a good answer, in words.

sliPercent.description: Good answers over the window, in percent (none: no answers yet).

targetPercent.description: The share of good answers aimed for, in percent.

SloStatus.description:
REQ: OBS-016 (ADR-105) — the service-level objectives, their error budgets, and how fast
they're being spent, over every node's answers.

enabled.description: `[slo] enabled`; when false there are no objectives.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that didn't answer (their answers aren't counted).

windowDays.description: Days each error budget covers (`[slo] window_days`).

cacheHitPercent.description: Cache share of answered queries that weren't blocked or local, 0–100.

latency.description: Latency percentiles this hour, by answer path (`cache`, `upstream`, ...).

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes that couldn't be read (CLU-002).

oneOf.description:
Present when client IPs appear masked (OPS-003): most recent queries come from a few
infrastructure addresses (a Kubernetes node, a Docker bridge, a forwarding router),
so per-device statistics and rules see those instead of devices.
Present when this node belongs to a cluster (CLU-001).

filterNames.description: Blocked names in the active snapshot.

filterSnapshot.description: Version of the active filter snapshot, if one is loaded.

oneOf.description: REQ: OPS-010 — this node's maintenance window, while it's in maintenance.

queryLog.description: Whether the per-query log is being written.

starts.description:
REQ: OBS-002 (T9.13) — times a node started on this data directory, and how many of
those followed a run that didn't stop cleanly.

update.description: Whether a newer build exists on this build's channel (ADR-046).

TailDropped.description: Sent as an SSE `dropped` event when matching queries weren't delivered.

dropped.description: How many matching queries were skipped since the last report.

reason.description: `rate`: over this subscriber's `rate`; `lag`: the subscriber fell behind.

byGroup.description: Queries by the client's group (ADR-050). Empty for buckets read from rollups.

slow.description:
REQ: OBS-016 — answered queries slower than the latency objective's threshold
(`[slo] latency_ms`). 0 in buckets stored by builds before 0.4.

upstreamQueries.description: Upstream exchanges, and how many failed.

group.description: For agent tokens: restricted to this client group.

ratePerMinute.description: For agent tokens: requests per minute (default: `[agents] rate_per_minute`).

scope.description: For user tokens. Agent tokens show the closest equivalent.

scopes.description: For agent tokens: what it may do (e.g. `analytics:read`, `config:write:clients`).

TokenKind.description: Whether a token is for a person's scripts or for an agent (AGT-004).

TopItem.description:
One ranked item. Counts come from a Space-Saving sketch: the true count lies in
`[count - errorBound, count]`.

groups.description:
For clients: the groups whose settings apply to it, highest priority first (its
device's groups, else its network's group, else the default; ADR-050).

name.description: The configured device name, for clients that have one.

secretBase32.description: For manual entry in an authenticator app.

UpdateStatus.description: Update status from the signed release index (ADR-046).

checkedUnixSeconds.description: When the index was last read successfully (Unix seconds).

how.description: How to update this install, step by step.

latest.description: The newest version on this channel, when known.

state.description:
`up_to_date`, `available`, `newer` (this build is newer than the index, e.g. dev),
`off` (`[updates] check = false`), or `unknown` (not checked yet, or failing).

password.description: Set a new password (ends the user's sessions).

resetTotp.description: Turn off the user's TOTP (if they lost their device).

UpstreamChecks.description:
REQ: OBS-019 (ADR-108) — one node's view of its upstreams' answers: second opinions
(sampled, `[upstream_check]`), DNSSEC verdicts, and the EDE codes they returned.

reference.description: The upstream group asked (none: another member of the answering group).

sampleEvery.description: One forwarded question in this many gets a second opinion.

UpstreamDisagreement.description: REQ: OBS-019 — two upstreams that answered the same question differently.

name.description: The name (hashed at privacy level 1 and above) and type.

UpstreamInfo.description: An upstream server and its health.

failuresByKind.description:
`failures` by kind, which say what to fix: timeouts point at the path or the upstream's
load, network errors at the connection, SERVFAIL at the domain asked about.

id.description: Stable ID (config order, from 1); query rows and latency rows refer to it.

UpstreamQuality.description: REQ: OBS-019 — one upstream's answers since start.

dnssecSecure.description: DNSSEC verdicts on its answers (when `[dnssec] mode` validates).

ede.description: The Extended DNS Error codes in its answers (RFC 8914).

same.description:
Second opinions by outcome: the same answer; different addresses (CDNs and geo-DNS
do this); a different response code; filtered (one side had addresses, the other none
or only 0.0.0.0/loopback); the second upstream didn't answer.

oidcProvider.description: The sign-in provider for users created by OIDC sign-in (they have no password here).

estimatedRows.description: Before scanning, from block headers: how many logged queries could match at most.

rowsScanned.description: What the scan did (0 for a dry run).

columns.description:
`time` (with `bucket`), the keys (a `client` key adds `clientName`), then the
statistics. Latencies are in ms.

missingNodes.description: Cluster nodes whose query log isn't here (not shipped to this node).

note.description: Something to know about the answer (a window longer than the query log keeps).

query.description: The query as understood, with the defaults filled in.

rows.description: One array per row, in column order.

source.description:
REQ: AGT-012 (T9.12) — where the numbers come from: `querylog` (every query, kept
`retention_days`) or `rollups` (counts by one breakdown, kept much longer).

truncated.description: The scan stopped early (`truncatedReason` says why); the numbers cover what it read.

ZoneInfo.description: REQ: DNS-018 (T7.22) — an authoritative zone from `[[zone]]`.

file.description: The zone file, when it has one.

groups.description: Groups that see it (split horizon); empty: everyone.

negativeTtlSeconds.description: TTL of its NXDOMAIN and no-data answers.

records.description: Records loaded (from the file and inline).

tags.name: stats
tags.description: Counters, top lists, and latency percentiles. Live windows in memory (15 minutes per second, 48 hours per minute) plus rollups on disk (7 days per minute, 400 days per hour, days forever).

tags.name: queries
tags.description: The query log and explanations of decisions.

tags.name: config
tags.description: Lists, groups, clients, and upstreams as running.

tags.name: agents
tags.description: Changes AI agents planned through MCP, and their approval.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Sign-in, two-factor, API tokens, and users. Everything else needs one of: the session cookie from POST /auth/login (plus X-CSRF-Token on changes), Authorization: Bearer <token>, or HTTP Basic for users who allow it.
